quote: Upfront, there's gonna be no cost. It's all gonna be so we have a bill swap program. We actually look at your power bill, and we replace it with a what's up?
stewart_read: The customer's 'what is this gonna cost me' is a direct match to the price_estimate_before_design trigger phrases. The canonical response redirects to gathering info for a real design rather than answering cost directly. The rep instead answers cost head-on with a blanket 'no cost' claim and launches into the bill-swap pitch before verify has even started, skipping the redirect strategy entirely.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged that a flat 'no upfront cost' reassurance was the fastest way to defuse a hostile opening — a reasonable read given the customer's abrupt tone — but the schema's canonical path exists precisely for this trigger and the rep never used it.
coaching_implication: Practice the redirect-to-design language for early, unprompted cost questions: acknowledge the fairness of the question, then bridge to 'the cost depends on your roof, usage, and offset — let me grab a few details and get you real numbers' instead of pre-answering cost before verify.

quote: that's we have to lower your bill and save you money in the first year or we can't offer it.
stewart_read: This is a compliance-relevant guarantee claim (a savings promise tied to program eligibility) delivered in a garbled, half-finished sentence. It is unclear from the rep's own delivery whether this is an accurate representation of Ion's program terms, and the customer has to ask for it to be repeated.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be reciting an approved compliance disclosure imperfectly rather than fabricating new claims, in which case this is a delivery/clarity issue rather than a knowledge gap about the underlying policy.
coaching_implication: Flag for the manager to verify this line against Ion's actual required disclosure language — if it is a scripted compliance statement, the rep needs to deliver it cleanly since the customer had to ask for a repeat, which erodes trust on an already-guarded call.

quote: Okay. I'm interested. Go ahead. Just to remind you, I'm on Social Security. I don't get that much money, and my house payment's over $1,000 a month.
stewart_read: This is a vulnerability disclosure (fixed income, financial strain) per the schema's trust-gift framing. The rep's response — 'Yeah. Okay. So So you're at 427 Marlborough Avenue?' — moves immediately into the address verify item with no acknowledgment of what she just shared.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be trying to keep momentum going while she is saying 'go ahead,' treating her statement as a permission-to-proceed rather than a disclosure requiring a pause — but the schema explicitly treats this category of disclosure as warranting acknowledgment before continuing.
coaching_implication: Coach a one-line acknowledgment before pivoting to verify questions on fixed-income disclosures — even a brief 'I hear you, that's exactly why we want to see if this can lower that bill' keeps the human moment intact without derailing the call.

quote: Okay. So how much is this gonna cost me altogether?
stewart_read: Second touch of the same cost objection; the rep again answers directly ('It's just gonna be a it's just gonna be a cheaper bill every month than what you're paying now. That's about it.') instead of using the design-redirect strategy.
alternative_hypothesis: Repeating the same reassurance could be a deliberate choice to keep the message simple and consistent for a customer who seems confused by the offer — consistency itself can build trust.
coaching_implication: Same rebuttal, second occurrence — this is the multi-touch signal the manager should replay with the rep to show the pattern, not just the single moment.

quote: Because you have to have a credit score over 670 to qualify for the program.
stewart_read: The rep states the 670 threshold accurately per the schema's stated policy, but the customer's answer relies entirely on self-reported bureau scores (650 TransUnion, 633 Equifax) that she flags herself as possibly wrong due to a disputed delinquency. The schema explicitly notes this exact scenario (qualifiers.credit_qualifier.policy_question_for_kenny) as an unresolved floor policy question — stated credit self-DQ vs. letting the closer's actual credit pull decide.
alternative_hypothesis: If Ion's resolved policy is that setters must DQ on stated credit, the rep followed correct procedure exactly and no coaching gap exists here at all.
coaching_implication: This moment's coaching value is contingent on Kenny resolving the stated-vs-pulled credit policy. Until then, flag it as a lead worth reviewing rather than a clear-cut rep error — the manager should confirm with Kenny whether this lead should have been passed to the closer's credit pull instead of self-DQ'd on the call.

quote: I guess I just have to call you back whenever my credit goes up, my my credit score.
stewart_read: The customer proposes her own vague future callback with no date or trigger attached, and the rep accepts it verbatim with no attempt to anchor a specific time, capture a callback date, or note the account for a future touch.
alternative_hypothesis: If the underlying credit-DQ is a hard, correct disqualification per Ion policy, there may be nothing left to anchor — the call genuinely ends here regardless of how it's closed.
coaching_implication: Even on a likely DQ, close with a concrete note-taking gesture ('let's put a reminder to check back in a few months') rather than letting the customer's own vague self-callback be the final word — this keeps the lead warm and recoverable.

quote: Hey. Sorry. Hey. Is this, Viola?
stewart_read: The rep's opening is halting and apologetic before confirming the customer's name, and only after this stumble does he state the company name and form reference at 00:06. This fumbled first five seconds likely contributes to the customer's immediate, unsoftened cost challenge at 00:13.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as a minor verbal tic rather than a legitimacy failure since the rep does recover and state 'this is Bucky with Ion... reaching out about the solar form' within the same breath.
coaching_implication: Coach a clean, confident opening line delivered without stumbling — the first five seconds set the tone the customer responds to for the rest of the call, and this call's guarded opening may trace directly back to it.
